generated.title: Chile 1960: The Strongest Earthquake Ever Recorded
generated.description:
On May 22, 1960, a magnitude 9.5 earthquake struck Chile: the largest ever recorded by instruments.

Here, the Nazca plate slides beneath South America. The plates had locked together, building stress, until the fault ruptured along hundreds of kilometers of the Chilean coast. The seafloor heaved upward and the ocean surged outward. About fifteen hours later tsunami waves reached Hawaii, where 61 people died in Hilo, and about twenty-two hours after the quake they reached Japan.

A tsunami can cross an entire ocean.

Part of the Historic Earthquakes series. Subscribe to Next Huge Quake for more earthquake science.
